Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) selects documents that are relevant to the query while being dissimilar to the documents already selected. The lambda parameter trades relevance against novelty, see section 4.
BM25 is a bag-of-words ranking function. It rewards term frequency with saturation (k1) and normalises by document length (b).
Language models use information at the beginning and end of a long context more reliably than information in the middle. Placing the most relevant passages at the edges improves answer accuracy.
Stuffing every retrieved chunk into the prompt wastes tokens and can push the most useful evidence out of the context window. Pack against an explicit token budget instead.
Retrievers often return overlapping chunks from the same document. Near-duplicate removal with shingled Jaccard similarity is cheap and removes most redundancy before ranking.
Chunk size is a trade-off: small chunks improve precision, large chunks preserve context. 300 to 800 tokens with a 10 to 15 percent overlap is a common starting point.
